evidence.field: 說文釋形；釋義；注音；漢語拼音
evidence.text: The entry records the received Shuowen analysis “論也。从言，吾聲,” with yǔ and yù readings. It cites Analects examples for “speak/discuss” and “tell” separately, and lists later extensions including language, literary wording, signals, and animal calls. These cited works are not dated here as surviving witnesses, so the list does not establish a chronological sense sequence.
evidence.title: [A03833] 語 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 國學大師字形演變資料
evidence.field: 字形演變；古文字字形說明
evidence.text: Search result text for this character reports bronze exemplars indexed 集成184 and 集成2840, and describes one early phonetic as a complex 五 form and the other as 吾; it says later analysis is 言 plus 吾. The page itself could not be reopened during this run, so this remains a reported account rather than independently inspected glyph evidence. It does not establish the early phonetic’s referent or name.

search_audit.query: 語 character Shuowen bronze forms glyph evolution Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang
search_audit.outcome: Search performed. The Xiaoxuetang URL opened without readable character content; the Ministry character entry opened and was inspected.
Search performed. Exact Commons descriptions for 言 and 吾 were opened; both provide exact original-image links and public-domain declarations.

gaps: This run did not establish a dated earliest surviving occurrence of 語 or date the extant witnesses behind the cited Analects uses. Dictionary ordering is not a chronology.

The reported early bronze phonetic variants, including the complex 五-shaped form, could not be checked against an opened character-specific paleography page or original inscription. Their original referents and pronunciations remain unestablished.
The chosen Commons images are modern redrawings in Shuowen seal style for component reference only; they do not depict the compound 語 or document its early bronze forms.

limitations.text: No verified direct glyph image of an early 語 inscription was established in this run; the search-result paleographic report could not be reopened, and the Xiaoxuetang character query returned no readable form record.
